open_points.subject: confirmation input binding digest
open_points.text: The pending confirmation keeps “the digest of its inputs in a fixed order”, while take_confirmation receives “the digest of its inputs”; no algorithm or unambiguous encoding of the structured inputs is fixed.
open_points.question: How are action inputs canonically encoded and digested, and which module computes the submission digest?
options: operations canonically encodes and digests the structured inputs before calling take_confirmation
take_confirmation receives the structured inputs and performs the canonical encoding and digest itself
open_points.default_guess: Have owner_sessions digest a specified length-delimited canonical encoding of the structured inputs with a specified cryptographic hash.

witness.initial: An owner session has a clean import mapping and no pending confirmation.
events: The owner asks for a confirmation step with one project's display name “ab” and alias “c”.
The browser submits the same confirmation value with display name “a” and alias “bc”.
outcomes: An implementation that digests plain fixed-order concatenation binds both inputs to the same bytes and accepts the changed import values.
An implementation using a length-delimited canonical encoding gets a different digest and refuses confirmation_bound_elsewhere.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees which display name and alias the imported project receives

open_points.subject: leftover store temporary file when the real store already exists
open_points.text: Observable effect says “A leftover file of the store's temporary name is removed”, but Errors refuses an unremovable leftover only “while the store is absent”; A17 likewise says the start fails on that removal failure only when the store is absent.
open_points.question: If a valid store exists but its leftover temporary file cannot be removed, does open_store continue with the existing store or fail the start?
options: Continue opening the existing store and leave the temporary file
Return a diagnostic and stop the start because the promised removal failed
open_points.default_guess: Continue with the existing valid store, following A17's explicit condition that removal failure stops the start only when the store is absent.

witness.initial: The configured location contains a valid store of the release's version and also its temporary-name file; permissions allow opening the store but prevent deleting the temporary file.
outcomes: Registry opens the existing store and starts, leaving the temporary file.
open_store returns a diagnostic because its specified removal effect failed, and Registry serves nothing.
witness.observer: The host operator and every caller waiting for Registry

open_points.subject: cookie expiry after concurrent session invalidation
open_points.text: The change requires expiry “on any answer to a request whose session is no longer valid”, while the operation says every check is operations' and exposes no result or owner_sessions capability by which the interface can learn that a successfully admitted request's session became invalid before its answer.
open_points.question: Is cookie expiry determined from validity at request admission, from a no_owner_session refusal, or from session validity again when the response is produced?
options: Expire only on sign-out responses and no_owner_session refusals
Recheck or receive a validity signal when producing every response and expire if the session has since ended
open_points.default_guess: Use response-time validity and provide the interface an explicit signal so it expires the cookie whenever the session has ended before headers are produced.

witness.initial: Owner session S is valid, and its browser has the session cookie.
events: Tab A starts a read using S and passes admit_owner_request.
While that read is running, Tab B signs out S.
A13 allows Tab A's admitted request to complete after the sign-out.
Tab A's answer is produced after S has ended.
outcomes: The cookie is expired on Tab A's response because S is no longer valid when the answer is sent.
The cookie is retained on Tab A's response because the request was valid when admitted and its answer is not a no_owner_session refusal.
witness.observer: The browser, which either removes the cookie or continues sending the stale cookie on later requests

set_aside.question: What does a successful check return when the operation is not on a project?
options: A successful result with no project value
set_aside.default_guess: Return a discriminated successful result whose project is absent for a session-only operation.
